dedupe_keys.name: dvgw netz und schadenstatistik wasser german water pipe network and damage statistics

description: The DVGW has collected data from German water utilities since 1997 on damage and its causes on supply pipes, house connections and network fittings, regulated since 2010 by the worksheet W 402, and publishes evaluations of the results. Utilities enter structure data such as water delivered, water losses and mean network age, plus pipe stock and damage data for mains, service and transmission lines and components, through a portal by web form, SOAP or CSV upload; the 2013 to 2015 evaluation used 1,098 data sets from 453 utilities. The statistics help utilities rate their performance, for benchmarks and competition cases, and plan rehabilitation under DVGW worksheets W 400-3 and W 403, and the DVGW notes the sample covers about one third of the national network and 45 percent of water delivered. Coverage: Germany, utility-level inputs published as aggregates. Access: free evaluation reports; raw data entry is by participating utilities and individual evaluations need the portal; the licence is not stated. Caveats: the sample is voluntary, and earlier optional fields were incomplete. It supports pipe failure and renewal modelling, and relates to the Korean national water supply information system record in the catalogue.
